voice_subtitles.config.title: Voice Subtitles
voice_subtitles.config.reset.tooltip: Put every setting back to its default.
voice_subtitles.config.no_cloth: Install Cloth Config for the richer settings screen
voice_subtitles.log.title: Conversation log
voice_subtitles.log.disclaimer: Speech is recognised automatically and can be wrong.
voice_subtitles.log.export_failed: Could not write the file – see the game log
voice_subtitles.log.hint: The log lives in memory and opens with /vsub log or a key of your choosing. Spoken lines come from automatic recognition, so it is a reminder of a conversation rather than a transcript of it; text chat lines are marked [chat] and are exact.
voice_subtitles.option.enabled.tooltip: Turn the subtitles off without removing the mod.
voice_subtitles.option.chat_placement.to: Where text chat subtitles appear – independent of voice.
voice_subtitles.option.show_self.tooltip: Also show what you say into your own microphone.
voice_subtitles.option.distance_fade.too: The further away a speaker is, the fainter their caption. Nothing is hidden: if you can hear it, you can read it.
voice_subtitles.option.far_opacity: Opacity at the edge of hearing
voice_subtitles.option.far_opacity.toolt: How faint a caption gets at the very edge of the speaker's range.
voice_subtitles.option.whisper_opacity.t: Whispers are drawn fainter than normal speech.
voice_subtitles.option.chat_strip_prefix: Drop the name from chat text
The server already prints the name in front of the message, and the subtitle prints it separately.
voice_subtitles.option.speech_enabled.to: Off leaves captions showing who is talking, without the words.
voice_subtitles.option.model_id.tooltip: Language code: ru, en, uk, de, fr, es, pl, it, ja. Empty follows the game language. Full list: /vsub model list.
voice_subtitles.option.auto_download.too: Fetches a model matching the game language on first run. Otherwise use /vsub model download.
voice_subtitles.option.show_partial.tool: Words appear as they are recognised, before the sentence ends.
voice_subtitles.option.max_recognizers.t: How many people are recognised at once. The rest get captions without words. Higher costs more CPU.
voice_subtitles.option.translation_mode: What to do about other languages
Off leaves everybody to your own model, which turns speech it does not know into nonsense. The other three each do one thing more.
voice_subtitles.option.my_language.toolt: Automatic follows the language the game is in, which is right nearly always.
voice_subtitles.option.default_spoken.to: Everybody except the people marked with /vsub lang. Automatic means the language you read, which is right on a server in your own language.
voice_subtitles.option.translate_chat.to: Writes the translation under the line it translates, in the chat itself. The only place a roleplay action can be translated: servers send those without saying who wrote them, so no caption is made for them.
voice_subtitles.option.show_original: Show what was said as well
voice_subtitles.option.show_original.too: The translation goes under the original rather than in place of it. On a roleplay server the wording is the evidence.
voice_subtitles.option.auto_download_tra: 113 MB the first time a language pair is needed. Everything stays on this machine.
voice_subtitles.option.translation.hint: Mark somebody as speaking another language with /vsub lang <player> <en|ru|reset>.
voice_subtitles.option.model.hint:
List models with /vsub model list, fetch one with /vsub model download <id>.

Russian, whole utterance (more accurate, a line arrives a second later): ru-giga-rnnt (GigaAM v3 by Sber, 162 MB, writes punctuation itself - the default), ru-giga (the same in CTC form), ru-big-int8 (57 MB, the accuracy of the big Vosk model).

Russian, streaming (words appear as they are said): ru-fast (23 MB), ru-stream (85 MB), ru-tone (123 MB, telephone speech).

English: en-fast (NVIDIA Parakeet, 103 MB, punctuation included - the default), en-heavy (Parakeet 0.6B, 465 MB, and 25 European languages including Russian).

Other languages on Vosk: uk, de, fr, es, pl, it, ja.

Whichever you pick, the mod fetches its engine once: sherpa-onnx (7-30 MB) or Vosk (25 MB).
voice_subtitles.option.name_source.toolt: The player list carries the roleplay name on servers that use one.
voice_subtitles.option.keep_server_style: Draw the name exactly as the server formats it, instead of recolouring it.
voice_subtitles.option.show_head.tooltip: Draw the speaker's face in front of their name.
voice_subtitles.option.color_speech.tool: Draw what was said in the speaker's colour.
voice_subtitles.option.color_names.toolt: Off by default: names keep the formatting the server gave them.
voice_subtitles.option.manual_colors.hin: Assign a colour by hand with /vsub color <player> <#RRGGBB>, or clear it with /vsub color <player> reset.
voice_subtitles.option.feed_alignment.to: Which side the feed sits on. Centred is the Story-Mode look; a side keeps the middle of the screen clear.
voice_subtitles.option.feed_anchor.toolt: Which edge the feed hangs from. Along the top it stays clear of the hotbar, the chat and everything else the bottom of the screen is already full of.
voice_subtitles.option.bottom_offset.too: How far above the bottom of the screen the feed sits.
voice_subtitles.option.top_offset.toolti: How far below the top of the screen the feed sits, when it hangs from the top.
voice_subtitles.option.max_width.tooltip: How much of the screen width the feed may take.
voice_subtitles.option.max_lines.tooltip: How many captions are visible at once.
voice_subtitles.option.lifetime.tooltip: How long a short line stays up. Longer lines stay longer – the time grows with the number of characters.
voice_subtitles.option.lifetime_per_char: How much longer each extra character keeps the line on screen.
voice_subtitles.option.lifetime_max.tool: Even the longest line goes no further than this.
voice_subtitles.option.background.toolti: How solid the dark plate behind the text is.
voice_subtitles.option.fade.tooltip: Captions fade rather than popping in and out.
voice_subtitles.option.show_direction.to: An arrow in front of the line shows where the speaker is standing: up for straight ahead, down for behind you. Captions carry the words but not the side the voice came from.
voice_subtitles.option.keep_log.tooltip: Holds what was said so it can be read back. Written to disk, in config/voice_subtitles/history, so it survives closing the game. Never sent anywhere.
voice_subtitles.option.log_capacity.tool: How many recent lines are kept to hand for reading and searching.
voice_subtitles.option.hide_with_hud.too: By default subtitles stay on screen when the interface is hidden – someone reading the conversation instead of hearing it should not lose it to a screenshot.
In hundredths of a block above the speaker's head.
voice_subtitles.option.over_head_width.t: Captions wrap once they reach this width.
voice_subtitles.option.over_head_walls.t: Like the voice it belongs to, which carries through walls too.
commands.voice_subtitles.help.lang: /vsub lang <player> <en|ru|reset> – say what language somebody speaks
commands.voice_subtitles.model.repair.no: Nothing has taken the game down, so there is nothing to repair
commands.voice_subtitles.model.repair.do: Threw away '%s'; it will be fetched again
commands.voice_subtitles.help.repair: /vsub model repair – fetch again whatever took the game down
commands.voice_subtitles.lang.cleared: %s speaks whatever everybody else here speaks
commands.voice_subtitles.lang.mode_off: Translation is off in the settings, so this changes nothing yet
commands.voice_subtitles.lang.none: Nobody has been marked as speaking anything else
commands.voice_subtitles.model.hint: /vsub model download <id> to fetch one, /vsub model use <id> to switch
commands.voice_subtitles.model.downloadi: Downloading model %s (%s MB). The game keeps running.
commands.voice_subtitles.model.missing: Model %1$s is not downloaded – /vsub model download %1$s
toast.voice_subtitles.native.failed: Voice Subtitles: could not download the sherpa-onnx library
toast.voice_subtitles.bundle.size: Unpacking what the mod was built with: %s MB
toast.voice_subtitles.bundle.ready.detai: Everything is in place; nothing was downloaded
voice_subtitles.bundle.unpacking: what the mod was built with

toast.voice_subtitles.translation.failed: The translation could not be downloaded
voice_subtitles.log.export.tooltip: Saves what is on screen, filters and all.
voice_subtitles.log.filter.speaker: Who: %s
voice_subtitles.option.log_keep_days.too: How long before old entries are deleted. Zero never deletes them.
voice_subtitles.log.clear.confirm: Press again to delete the log
voice_subtitles.option.log_events.toolti: Marks joining and leaving a server, deaths and closing the game in the log. Without them the log is a wall of speech with no idea where or when any of it happened.
voice_subtitles.log.tampered: The log file was altered outside the game; some entries are not shown
voice_subtitles.option.fade_millis.toolt: How long a caption takes to arrive. Leaving takes about twice as long: going should be less abrupt than coming.
voice_subtitles.option.typewriter.toolti: Recognised words appear a few characters at a time rather than in whole jumps. Nothing is delayed by it: the typing outruns the speaking, and if it ever falls behind it shows everything at once.
voice_subtitles.option.over_head_rows.to: No more than this, showing the most recent rows. Otherwise long speech grows downwards until it reaches the floor.
voice_subtitles.option.over_head_backgro: How solid the dark plate behind the text is.
voice_subtitles.option.over_head_name.to: Show the speaker's name in front of their words.
voice_subtitles.option.log_chat.tooltip: Puts everything the chat showed in the log: server announcements, other people's commands, the results of roleplay. Those lines are marked [CHAT].
voice_subtitles.option.hide_command_resu: Keeps the server's answer to your own roleplay command out of the captions: a dice roll is not speech, and it is already in the chat and in the log.
voice_subtitles.preview.text.1: This is what a caption looks like: the words appear as the speech is recognised, then the line fades away.
voice_subtitles.preview.text.2: Ask for another while this one is still up and you will see both halves of the motion at once.
voice_subtitles.preview.text.3: Wrapping width, text size and the darkness of the plate are set in the same place as everything else.
voice_subtitles.preview.text.4: A long enough line stays up longer than a short one, so there is time to read it to the end.
